steps.comment: SpeedLM: a vLLM server that retrains its own speculative decoder while idle.
this is how you serve Qwen3-8B on plain vLLM.
this is SpeedLM. same server, same model, one added flag.
that flag is running right now, as SLURM job 380450.
it needs traffic first. we drove 430 real agentic-coding trajectories at it.
that left a corpus of real request/response records -- nothing synthetic.
then the traffic stopped. the tuner noticed, slept vLLM, and took the GPU.
it rendered training rows out of a 1024-record window and started fitting.
every loss below is being written by the trainer, live, as you watch it.
steps.command: timeout 7200 tail --pid=$(pgrep -f speculators/scripts/train.py | head -1) -F -n +1 "$L" 2>/dev/null | grep --line-buffered -oE 'epoch [0-9]+/8 started|train/loss=[0-9.]+|val/loss_epoch=[0-9.]+, epoch=[0-9]+'

steps.comment: training done. now the gate -- is it actually faster, and does it still agree?
steps.command: timeout 5400 tail -F -n +1 $H/runs/events.jsonl | jq --unbuffered -r '"\(.from) -> \(.to)   \(.reason)"' | stdbuf -oL awk '{print substr($0,1,96)} /-> READY/&&NR>1{exit}'

steps.comment: and the numbers the gate decided on -- measured, not claimed.
quality passed. but the speed number has to hold still to count -- it did not.
candidate tok/s climbed every repeat while stock sat flat. so: rolled back.
one flag. the server tuned itself, measured itself, and refused its own win.
